topology_reasoning: The bitmap is a device-only black-on-white MZI-like layout on layer (1,0), with the material bbox equal to the supplied 91.1 um by 50.75 um footprint.
The left side is a narrow input taper into a compact rectangular multimode splitter. Immediately after that rectangle the material separates into two close, parallel waveguide outputs.
Those two outputs become smooth routed arms: the upper arm rises to the top footprint edge, runs horizontally through the middle of the device, and returns to the upper input of the right combiner.
The lower arm mirrors the topology but extends farther downward than the upper arm extends upward from the splitter axis, creating the MZI path-length imbalance.
The right side is the mirror of the left: two close waveguide inputs taper into a compact rectangular combiner and then into a narrow output taper.
The reconstruction should therefore use only tapers, rectangles, and two extruded gf.Path centerlines; no prebuilt MZI, coupler, or raw polygon stencil is needed.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitive reconstruction using taper/rectangle splitter-combiner sections and explicit Euler-path top/bottom arms.
Narrowed routed waveguide width and split tapers to reduce false-positive material from iteration 1.
Increased Euler bend extent to shorten the vertical flats and better match the turn regions.
Replaced symmetric Euler arms with cubic gf.Path centerlines fitted to the bitmap turn topology while preserving delta_length as lower-arm vertical extension.
Moved the inner turn point outward and the outer turn point inward to tighten the vertical-side match.
Slightly relaxed the inner turn point, lowered the outer turn point, and widened split taper mouths; kept this as the best of six iterations.
